data.narrative:
Wayve is a Series D autonomous systems company founded by Amar Shah and Alex Kendall, currently valued at $8.6B post-money following $1.5B in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws from a peer set of eight private companies in the Drones & Autonomous sector, with particular focus on four same-tier comparables: Zipline ($7.6B Series G), Joby Aviation ($6.9B public), Nuro ($6.0B Series G), and Archer Aviation ($3.3B public).

Two triangulation methods are applicable here. The stage-progression method applies a typical 1.5x step-up multiplier from Series D to next-stage funding, yielding $12.9B. The peer-median method examines the four comparable valuations above, establishing a median of $6.4B with a range of $3.3B to $7.6B. This peer sample reflects mixed-stage maturity—two publicly traded, two late-private—introducing valuation variance tied to liquidity and market conditions.

The triangulated analysis produces a range of $5.5B (low) to $14.8B (high), with a median of $9.7B. The $8.6B current valuation sits below the median estimate, suggesting modest upside within the range. Key uncertainties include path-to-revenue timing, the valuation delta between private late-stage and public exits in autonomous systems, and sector-specific regulatory risk not quantified in peer comparables.
